algorithm.hash: sha-256 over one record per input
algorithm.host_invariance: the logical name is why one source state has one identity: hashing the build host's own path string instead makes the value differ between a POSIX and a Windows checkout
algorithm.input_order: Cargo.toml first, then every .rs file under src, sorted by logical name
algorithm.logical_name: the file path split on both the POSIX and the Windows separator, empty and '.' components dropped, remaining components joined by '/'

measured_without_the_normalizer.note: the two digests below are what the pre-normalizer build.rs produces from this same source state: equal on a POSIX host and different for a Windows host, which is the defect this record guards against

purpose: Expected IPRANGE_V4_BUILD_ID for one source state, per build host. The Rust CLI and the iprange-v4-worker compare this identity during the worker handshake, so a host-dependent value cannot attest that two binaries came from one tree. Each native run checks its own platform entry against the binary it built.
regenerate_with: python3 v4/cli/command_sanitize.py --emit-build-ids v4/cli/evidence/build-ids.json --built-cli <release iprange> --built-worker <release iprange-v4-worker>; the digest is recomputed from v4/rust/iprange-livedb/Cargo.toml and every .rs file under v4/rust/iprange-livedb/src

source_state.note: the value is a pure function of iprange-livedb's Cargo.toml and src/**.rs content; any change under that package regenerates it. Regenerate this file whenever the package changes and never hand-edit a digest.

verified_against_built_products.method: the recomputed digest is searched for verbatim in the bytes of the named built executables
